Μωσῆς γοῦν προφητεύων περὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ προφήτην μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξαιρέτως εἶπεν εἰπών· «προξήτην ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ὑμῶν ἀναστήσει ὑμῖν κύριος ό θεὸς ὡς ἐμέ, αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔσται, ὃς ἂν μὴ ἀκούσῃ τοῦ προφήτου ἐκείνου ἐξολοθρευθήσεται ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ. οὑτος οὖν έστιν ὁ καὶ προφήτης «εἰς ἔθνη« τεθειμένος καὶ ἔλαβε χάριν ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἐκχυθεῖσαν ἐν τοῖς χείλεσιν αὐτοῦ, ἴνα μὴ μόνον, ὅτε παρῆν τῷ οώματι, ἀλλὰ καὶ νῦν, ὅτε πάρεστι δυνάμει καὶ τῷ πνεύματι, προφητεύῃ «ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη«, ὥστε ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν Μνῶν ἀνύειν αὐτοῦ τὴν προφητείαν καὶ ἕλκειν ἀνθρώπους ἐπὶ σωτηρίαν.
english: 'I have set you as a prophet to the nations.' (Jeremiah 1:5) If you look for this in Jeremiah — 'I have set you as a prophet to the nations' (Deuteronomy 18:15) — watch later on: he is commanded to prophesy 'against all the nations,' (Jeremiah 48:1) and there is a heading, 'What Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations,' (Deuteronomy 18:19) against Elam, against Damascus, against Moab. And we have it that he 'prophesied against all the nations,' (Jeremiah 25:13) as regards the letter of 'I have set you as a prophet to the nations,' (Jeremiah 49:34) said to him.

If it is a matter of the higher sense: if of Jeremiah, we have already spoken; if of the Savior, what need is there even to say it? He truly prophesied to all the nations. For he is, as he is ten thousand other things, also a prophet. As he is high priest, as he is savior, as he is physician, so he is also prophet. Moses, prophesying about him, did not say only 'a prophet,' but said it with a special force: 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from your brothers, like me (Deuteronomy 18:15); him you shall hear, and it shall be that whoever does not hear that prophet shall be destroyed from his people.' (Jeremiah 49:23)

This one, then, is also the prophet set 'to the nations,' and he received grace from God poured out on his lips, so that not only when he was present in the body, but also now, when he is present in power and in the Spirit, he may prophesy 'to all the nations,' so that from all the nations his prophecy may reach its end and draw men to salvation (Acts 3:22–23) (Psalm 45:2).

source_text: «Καὶ εἶπα· ὁ ὤν δέσποτα κύριε, ἰδοὺ οὐκ ἐπίσταμαι λαλεῖν ὅτι νεώτερος ἐηώ εἰμι. καὶ εἶπε κύριος πρός με· μὴ λέγε ὅτι νεώτερος ἐγώ εἰμι, ὅτι πρὸς πάντας οὓς ἐὰν ἐξαποστείλω σε πολλάκις εἴπομεν, ὅτι ἔστι κατὰ τὸν ἔσω ἄνθρωπον εἶναι παιδίον, κἂν ἐν γεροντικῇ τις ᾖ ἡλικίᾳ σώματος· ἔστι δέ ποτε κατὰ τὸν ἔξω ἄνθρωπον εἶναι παιδίον, κατὰ δὲ τὸν ἔσω ἄνδρα. τοιοῦτος ἦν ὁ Ἱερεμίας, ἤδη ἔχων τὴν χάριν ἀπὸ θεοῦ ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ τοῦ παιδίου ἡλικίᾳ κατὰ τὸ σῶμα. διό φησιν αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος· «μὴ λέγε ὅτι νεώτερος ἐγώ εἰμι. σημεῖον δὲ τοῦ μῆ εἶναι αὐτὸν νεώτερον, ἀλλ᾿ «ἄνδρα τέλειον«, τὸ «πρὸς πάντας οὃς ἐὰν ἐξαποστείλω σε πορεύσῃ, καὶ κατὰ πάντα ὅσα ἐὰν ἐντείλωμαί σοι λαλήσεις. μὴ φοβηθῇς ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτῶν. οὖδεν ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος ὅτι οἱ πρεσβεύοντες τὸν λόγον κινδυνεύουσιν ἐν τοῖς ἀκούουσιν· ἐλεγχόμενοι γὰρ μισοῦσιν αὐτούς, ἐπιπλησσόμενοι διώκουσι. πᾶν ὁτιοῦν πάσχουσιν οἱ προφῆται· «οὐκ ἔστι προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ ἰδίᾳ πατρίδι καὶ τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ. οὗ καὶ πρώην ἐμνημονεύομεν. οἶδεν οὖν ὁ θεὸς πέμπων τὸν προφήτην, ὅσους κινδύνους ἀναδέξεται, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· «μὴ φοβηθῇς ἀπὸ προσώπου αὐτῶν, ὅτι μετὰ σοῦ εἰμι τοῦ ἐξαιρεῖσθαί σε, λέγει κύ- ριος. ἃ πέπονθεν Ἱερεμίας, ἀναγέγραπται· εἰς λάκκον βορβόρου βέβληται, ἔμεινεν ἐκεῖ >ἕνα ἄρτον ἐσθίων τῆς ἡμέρας< καὶ ὕδωρ μόνον πίνων, καὶ ἄλλα δὲ μυρία ἃ πέπονθεν ἡ προφητεία αὐτοῦ δεδήλωκεν. «τίνα τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἐδίωξαν οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν«; εἴρηται πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους. καὶ ἀναγκαῖόν ἐστι >τοὺς θέλοντας ζῆν εὐ- σεβῶς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ πάντως ὑπὸ δυνάμεων ἀντικειμένων δι᾿ ὧν εὑρίσκουσι σκεῦῶν διώκεσθαι<. διὰ τοῦτο μὴ ξενιζόμενοι οἱ διωκόμενοι πάντα πραττέτωσαν, μόνον εὐχόμενοι, ἵνα ἀδίκως διώκωνται καὶ μὴ δικαίως, μὴ δι᾿ ἀδικίαν, μὴ δι᾿ ἁμαρτίαν, μὴ διὰ πλεονεξίαν.

ἐὰν δὲ διώκηταί ποτέ τις διὰ δικαιοσύνην, καὶ ἀκουέτω τοῦ «μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν ὀνειδίζωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ διώκωσι καὶ εἴπωσι πᾶν πονηρὸν ῥῆμα καθ᾿ ὑμῶν ψευδόμενοι ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ. χαίρετε καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὅτι ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· οὕτως γὰρ ἐδίωξαν τοὺς προφήτας τοὺς πρὸ ὑμῶν.
english: 'And I said, You who are, Master, Lord, behold, I do not know how to speak, because I am younger. And the Lord said to me, Do not say that I am younger, because to all to whom I send you...' (Jeremiah 1:6–8) We have often said that it is possible, according to the inner man, to be a child, even if someone is in an old age of body. And it is possible at times, according to the outer man, to be a child, and according to the inner, a man. Such was Jeremiah, already having the grace from God while he was still in the age of a child according to the body. That is why the Lord says to him, 'Do not say that I am younger.' (Ephesians 4:13) And a sign that he is not younger, but 'a grown man,' is this: 'To all to whom I send you, you shall go, and according to all that I command you, you shall speak. Do not be afraid of their face.' (Matthew 13:57)

The Word of God knows that those who serve as ambassadors of the word are in danger among the hearers. For when they are exposed they hate them; when they are rebuked they persecute them. The prophets suffer every kind of thing. 'A prophet is not without honor except in his own country and in his house' (Jeremiah 38:6–9) — which we also recalled earlier. So God, sending the prophet, knows how many dangers he will take on, and he says to him, 'Do not be afraid of their face, because I am with you to deliver you, says the Lord.' (Jeremiah 37:21)

What Jeremiah suffered is written down. He was thrown into a pit of mire; he remained there eating one loaf a day and drinking water only; and ten thousand other things which his prophecy has made clear. 'Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute?' (Acts 7:52) it is said to the Jews. And it is necessary that 'those who want to live in a godly way in Christ Jesus be persecuted in every case by opposing powers, through the vessels they find.' (2 Timothy 3:12) Therefore those who are persecuted must not be surprised, but must do everything, only praying that they be persecuted unjustly and not justly — not for injustice, not for sin, not for greed. And if someone is ever persecuted for righteousness, let him also hear, 'Blessed are you when they reproach you and persecute you and say every evil word against you, lying, for my sake (Matthew 5:11). Rejoice and be glad, because your reward is great in the heavens; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.' (Matthew 5:10–12) (2 Corinthians 4:16)

english: After this let us look at: 'If you wash yourself with nitre and multiply soap for yourself, you are stained in your injustices before me, says the Lord.' (Jeremiah 2:22) Did some sinning soul suppose that, taking nitre and washing with ordinary nitre, it ceases from the stain and ceases from the sin? Did someone assume that, taking this herb that springs from the earth and washing and scouring, the soul is cleansed, because the Word says here to the one who has turned into bitterness and become an alien vine, 'If you wash yourself with nitre and multiply soap for yourself, you are stained in your injustices before me, says the Lord' (Hebrews 4:12)?

But one must know that the Word has all power. And as he has the power of all Scripture, so the Word has the power of every medicine, and is the power of everything that cleanses, and is most scouring. 'For the word of God is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword.' (Isaiah 1:6–7) And whatever you name, of which there is need, that is in the power of the Word. So there is a word that is nitre, and there is a word that is soap, which, when spoken, cleanses such filth. But since not every sin is healed from such a word as is nitre, and from such a word as is soap — there are sins that do not need nitre or soap — it is said to the one who thinks it has sins of a kind that can be washed off in nitre and soap: 'If you wash yourself with nitre and multiply soap for yourself, you are stained before me in your injustices, says the Lord.' (Isaiah 4:4)

And as of wounds some are healed with a poultice, and others with oil, and others need a bandage and so are made well, and there are other wounds of which it is said, 'There is no poultice to put on, nor oil nor bandages; but your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire' (1 John 5:16) — so there are some sins which soil the soul, and for these sins the man needs a word that is nitre, a word that is soap. And there are some sins which are not healed this way, for they are not even compared to soil. That is why the Lord in Isaiah, knowing the differences of sins, see how he says, 'The Lord will wash the soil of the sons and of the daughters of Zion, and he will cleanse the blood from their midst with a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning.' Soil and blood: soil with a spirit of judgment, blood with a spirit of burning. If you have sinned, yet not 'unto death,' you have been soiled. So 'the Lord will wash the soil of the sons and of the daughters of Zion, and he will cleanse the blood from their midst.' (Isaiah 4:4) Then the matching: toward 'the soil,' 'with a spirit of judgment'; toward 'the blood,' 'with a spirit of burning.' And most of us, if we have sinned the worse things, do not need nitre, nor the multiplying of soap, but the spirit of burning.

english: Acts says it plainly: the apostles went first into the synagogues of the Jews. They announced to them, as kin through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, what Scripture had written about the coming of Jesus Christ.

When those hearers would not receive what was said, others had to hear it. So the apostles made their defense and left them. Scripture records: 'It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first. Since you judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look—we turn to the Gentiles.'

What Acts states with force in many places the prophets also said. The Holy Spirit speaks first through the holy prophets to that people. But when much has been spoken and not heard, the Spirit prophesies the word that will be preached to the nations.

The same turn happens at the start of today's reading. Before this, Israel heard: 'Even if you call me Father and do not turn away from me, yet as a woman deals treacherously with her companion, so the house of Israel has dealt treacherously with me,' says the Lord. And they heard that they had done wrong in their ways and forgotten their holy God. Then the Holy Spirit shifts the word to us who come from the nations and says: 'Return, you turning children, and I will heal your broken places.'

We are the ones filled with broken places. Each of us could say, even if now cleansed and healed: 'We too were once foolish, led astray, enslaved to many and varied desires and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hated and hating one another (Titus 3:3). But when the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared, he poured out his mercy on us through the washing of rebirth.'

Paul, an apostle from Israel—blameless according to the righteousness in the law—does not say only that the nations were once foolish. He says, 'We also were once disobedient and foolish.' Not only those from the nations were foolish, not only they were disobedient and sinful. We who were taught the law were the same before Christ's coming. So after the words addressed to Israel, the word turns to us from the nations: 'Return, you turning children, and I will heal your broken places.'

english: Someone will object: 'Those words were spoken to Israel, yet you drag them over to people from the nations.' We want to show that whenever God means to speak to Israel about turning back, he does not wait long—he adds Israel's name at once.

Next it says: 'If Israel returns to me, says the Lord, he will return; if he removes his abominations from his mouth and stands in awe before my face and swears, “As the Lord lives,” in truth, judgment, and righteousness, then nations will bless themselves in him.' So the earlier words were spoken to those from the nations. For when the fullness of the nations enters, then all Israel will be saved, as the apostle writes to the Romans.

See how God urges us who are turning to turn completely. He promises that if we turn to him as people who turn, he will heal our broken places through Jesus Christ. We answer—not delaying over salvation as that Israel did—'Here we are; we will be yours.'

God said, 'Return, you turning children, and I will heal your broken places.' Those from the nations reply that we will be his servants. We were not his before; we belonged to demons and opposing powers. When the Most High divided the nations, we did not become his portion or Jacob's inheritance allotment; we became portions of others. Yet when he said to us, 'Return, you turning children, and I will heal your broken places,' we who once were other portions answer, 'Here we are.' This is the call we were waiting for. They were called and refused; we who are called do not refuse in the same way.

In the Gospel parables some of those first invited said, 'I have married a wife; excuse me,' and another, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen and am going to test them (Luke 14:19); excuse me.' We from the nations are not called and then refuse like that. Over what field would we settle? Over what wise wife? Over what else would we busy ourselves? God has said to us, 'Return, you turning children, and I will heal your broken places.' Seeing our broken places and the promise of healing, we answer at once: 'Look—we will be yours, for you are the Lord our God.'

Having heard and said, 'We will be yours,' let us remember that we promised God that very thing. Having said it, let us become nothing else—not a spirit of anger, not a spirit of grief, not a spirit of desire, not the devil, not his angels. Called, and having said, 'Look—we will be yours,' let us show to those left desolate that we have dedicated ourselves to him alone. We say, 'For you are the Lord our God.' We confess no other god—not the belly, as gluttons do, 'whose god is the belly'; not silver, as the greedy do, nor greed, which is idolatry; nor anything else that many deify. For us the God over all is God—over all, through all, and in all. Because love binds us to God, we say: 'Here we are; we will be yours, for you are the Lord our God.'

english: He adds: 'And nations will bless themselves in him, and in him they will praise God in Jerusalem. For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and to those who dwell in Jerusalem.' (Genesis 12:3; 18:18; 22:18; 26:4) He has spoken to those from the nations, and he has spoken to those from Israel; he speaks to those from Judah. I remember the figurative readings said earlier about Judah and those dwelling in Jerusalem. For we dwell—if God grants—in Jerusalem.

Since 'where the treasure is, there the heart is also,' (Galatians 4:26) if we store up treasure in heaven, we also have the heart in the Jerusalem above, about which the apostle says: 'But the Jerusalem above is free, which is our mother,' (Luke 9:62) as it is written, and what follows. So 'thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and to those who dwell in Jerusalem: Break new ground for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.' (1 Corinthians 3:6) This word is spoken especially to those who teach, so that they not entrust what is said to the hearers before they make new ground in their souls. For when, putting hand to the plow, they make new ground in souls—according to the good and fine soil of those who hear—then as they sow they do not sow among thorns.

But if, before the plow and before making new ground in the ruling principle of the hearers, someone takes the holy seeds—the word about the Father, about the Son, about the Holy Spirit, about resurrection, about punishment, about rest, about law, about prophets, and in short about each of the things written—and sows them, he transgresses the command that says first, 'Break new ground for yourselves,' and second, 'Do not sow among thorns.'

But one of the hearers will say: 'I do not teach; I am not under this command.' You too become a farmer of yourself, and do not sow among thorns, but make new ground for me in the plot God of all has entrusted to you. Consider the plot; see where the thorns are—where cares of life and deceit of wealth and love of pleasure are. Having seen the thorns in your soul, seek the rational plow about which Jesus says, 'No one who puts hand to the plow and turns back is fit for the kingdom of God.' Having sought it and found it, gathering from the Scriptures the pure working oxen, plow and renew the land, and so that it may no longer be old, make it new—putting off the old man with his practices and putting on the new man renewed into knowledge. You will make new ground for yourself, and if you make the new ground, take seeds from those who teach, take seeds from the law, from the prophets, from the Gospel writings, from the apostolic words, and having taken these seeds sow the soul through memory and study. They will seem to spring up of themselves; but in truth after the memory of them it is not they that spring up, but God who grows them: 'I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the growth.' (1 Corinthians 3:6) And if anyone has been able to understand the Scriptures, that one has made new ground, and having made it has sown not among thorns. These seeds are managed by God not to become an ear all at once, but as in the Gospel according to Mark: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain.

When it is ready for harvest, those sent out upon the harvest will come. When it is ready for harvest, they will come to whom the word says: 'Lift up your eyes and see the fields, that they are already white for harvest.' So he says to us: 'Break new ground for yourselves, and do not sow among thorns.' But if, before you cleanse your soul, while you still have thorns, you approach one who can teach or is thought to teach, or ask for lessons and spiritual seeds, you transgress the command that says, 'Do not sow among thorns.'

(Numbers 10:2–3) The lofty word—the one that wakes the hearer, that prepares him for the fight against the passions and against the activities of opposing powers, that prepares him for the heavenly festivals (for it is said with a view to both)—is taken as a trumpet.

In Numbers such a word is a trumpet. For example, the word commands me—and anyone else to whom it is given who wills and has sought the mind of the Scriptures—to make 'silver trumpets, hammered work.' So the word says: 'Signal with a trumpet upon the earth, and cry aloud; say: Gather yourselves and let us enter the walled cities.' (Jeremiah 4:7) The word of God does not want us to enter an unwalled city, but into the church of the living God, walled by the strength of the Word—for he is the wall. In the seventeenth Psalm it also lies that God is a wall. 'Taking it up, flee into Zion.' As many of you as are outside Zion, 'taking it up, flee into Zion; hurry, do not stand still.' (Psalm 9:11 (LXX)) You who are in progress, hurry to the Lookout, 'for I am bringing evils from the north and a great crushing' (Psalm 139:12 (LXX))—evils brought 'from the north'—from the opposing one, the north, as has often been said. Whoever is found not hurrying and not entering 'into the walled cities,' not becoming 'in the churches of God,' but standing outside, will himself be caught by the enemies and destroyed. Who is the enemy? Let us see from what follows how it is said: 'A lion has gone up from his den; destroying nations he has carried them off.' This is the enemy we must flee. A lion pursues us. Who is this? Peter teaches, saying: 'Your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion seeking whom he may swallow (1 Peter 5:8); resist him, firm in the faith.' And according to the ninth Psalm he 'lies in wait in secret; he lies in wait like a lion in his den.' And this lion does not lie in wait by day, but when night has come. For according to the hundred-and-third Psalm: 'You set darkness, and it became night. In it all the beasts of the wood will pass through, young lions roaring to snatch and to seek from God food for themselves.'

ὁρᾷς πῶς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἀνάγει ὁ θεὸς καὶ σωματοποιεῖ τὰς νεφέλας; διὰ τοῦτο εἰ βουλόμεθα γενέσθαι νεφέλαι, ἐφ' ἃς φθάνει ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ θεοῦ, ἔσχατοι πάντων γενώμεθα καὶ εἴπωμεν ἔργοις καὶ διαθέσει τὸ «δοκῶ γάρ, ὁ θεὸς ἡμᾶς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ἐσχάτους ἀπέδειξεν( κἂν μὴ ἀπόστολος ὦ, ἔξεστί μοι γενέσθαι ἐσχάτῳ, ἵνα ὁ θεὸς ἀνάγων νεφέλας 241r | ἀπ' «ἐσχάτου τῆς γῆς« ἀναγάγῃ με. «Καὶ ἀστραπὰς εἰς ὑετὸν ἐποίησεν. λέγουσιν οἱ περὶ ταῦτα δεινοί, ὅτι ἡ γένεσις τῶν ἀστραπῶν ἀπὸ τῶν νεφελῶν γίνεται ἀλλή- λαις προστριβομένων.

ὅπερ γὰρ συμβαίνει περὶ τοὺς πυροβόλους λί- θους ἐπὶ γῆς, ἕνα δύο λίθων προσκρουσάντων πῦρ γενγθῇ, τοῦτο γίνεσθαι καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν φασιν. προσκρουομένων τῶν νεφελῶν κατὰ τοὺς χειμῶνας γίνεται ἡ ἀστραπή. διὸ ὡς ἐπίπαν ἡ άστραπὴ ἅμα βροντῇ γίνεται, τῆς μὲν βροντῆς ἐμφαινούσης τὸν ἡχον τοῦ συγ- κρουσμοῦ τῶν νεφελῶν, τῆς δὲ ἀστραπῆς γεννώσης τὸ φῶς.
english: If we have considered what the clouds are, let us see how God draws up clouds from the farthest part of the earth. How “from the farthest part of the earth”? The Savior says: “Whoever wishes to be first among you shall be last of all.” Paul observed this commandment and became last in this world; therefore he says: “I think that God has displayed us the apostles last, as condemned to death, for we have become a spectacle to the world and to angels and to human beings.” (1 Corinthians 4:9) Therefore whoever keeps the Savior’s commandment and becomes last as regards this life becomes a cloud; and God draws up clouds not from the first of the earth, nor from consuls, nor from rulers, nor from the rich—for “Blessed are the poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.” You see how God draws up from the last and forms the clouds into bodies. Therefore if we wish to become clouds upon which God’s truth reaches, we must become last of all and declare in work and disposition: “I think that God has displayed us the apostles last” (even if I am not an apostle, it is permitted for me to become last, so that God, drawing up clouds from “the farthest part of the earth,” may draw me up). And he made lightnings for rain. Those clever about these things say that the generation of lightning comes to be from clouds rubbing against one another.

For just as it happens with fiery stones thrown upon the earth—when one or two stones strike each other and fire is kindled—so they say it happens with the clouds: when the clouds strike together in winter, lightning comes to be. Hence, as lightning always comes to be together with thunder, the thunder manifests the sound of the clouds’ collision, and the lightning produces the light.

english: If you have understood the example, look also at the intelligible cloud. Moses was a cloud; Joshua son of Nun was a cloud. These two speak to one another, and from their words lightning comes. Jeremiah was a cloud; Baruch was a cloud. They converse with each other, and lightning came from Jeremiah’s words and from Baruch’s words. So if you are able, gather from the writings how lightning comes. And in the new covenant Paul and Silvanus were two clouds.

They came together, and the lightning of the letter occurred. “Lightnings,” therefore, God “made into rain and brought forth winds from his treasuries.” Are these winds, then, in the treasuries? Or does it not appear how their nature, blowing upon the earth, subsists? But there are treasuries of winds, treasuries of spirits: “spirit of wisdom and understanding, spirit of counsel and might, spirit of knowledge and godliness,” “spirit of the fear of the Lord,” “spirit of power and love and a sound mind.” And you yourself are able from the writings to gather these winds. These spirits are in the treasuries. What are the treasuries? “In whom are hid the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” These treasuries are in Christ.

Therefore from there come these winds, these spirits, that one may be wise, another faithful, another having knowledge, another having received some gift of God. “For to one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit, and to another faith in the same Spirit.” (1 Corinthians 12:8–9)

english: We have become God's people, and the righteousness of God is to the people from the nations. For this is the people that is born in entirety, and it is said in the prophet: 'If a nation was born once, a nation was born once when the savior appeared and thousands believed in one day, and were added on another day three thousand. And it is seen that the whole people is born by the word of God and the barren woman, who previously did not bear, is being born in entirety, to whom it is said: 'Rejoice, barren one who does not bear, break forth and cry, you who do not wail, for many are the children of the desolate rather than of the one who has a husband.' (Isaiah 54:1) The desolate is the church; the desolate is God's law. The one who has a husband is that synagogue which is called the congregation.

What then does God promise me? 'You shall be to me a people, and I shall be to you a God.' Not all are God, but only those to whom He grants Himself, as He granted Himself to that patriarch to whom He said, 'I am your God,' and again to another, 'I shall be your God,' and concerning others, 'I shall be their God.' When then do we attain, as I say individually, to being His God? If you wish to know what God is and to whom He grants His name, He is the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob. And the Savior says this: 'God is not of the dead but of the living.' Who is the dead? The sinner, the one not having the one who spoke.

I am the one having dead works, the one not yet having repented from dead works, about which the apostle says: 'Do not lay again a foundation of repentance from dead works.' If then 'God is not a God of the dead but of the living,' and we know who is the living, because the one living according to Christ and remaining with Him, if we desire one of us to be God, we will put away the works of death, that He may fulfill His promise saying: 'And I shall be to you a God, that I may establish my oath which I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey.' For He says: 'I shall establish my oath which I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey,' as not yet having given them the 'land flowing with milk and honey.' For this is not the land which God said 'flowing with milk and honey,' but that which the Savior taught saying: 'Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the land.'

Ταύτα ὁ προφήτης. εἶτα ὁ σωτὴρ ἐν τῷ προφήτῃ ἴδωμεν τίνα λέγει· «ἐγὼ ὡς ἀρνίον ἄκακον ἀγόμενον τοῦ θύεσθαι οὐκ ἔγνων. ἐπ ἐμὲ ἐλογίσαντο λογισμόν, λέγοντες· δεῦτε καὶ ἐμβάλωμεν ξύλον εἰς τὸν ἄρτον αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκτρίψωμεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ γῆς ζώντων, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ οὐ μὴ μνησθῇ ἐτι. ὡς φησὶν καὶ ὁ προφήτης Ἡσαΐας, Χριστὸς «ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.

english: If divine words are present in the Law and Prophets, and also in the Gospels and Apostles, the one being taught must have God as the teacher of divine words, for God is the one who teaches knowledge, as written in Psalms. The Savior also testifies that no one should be called a teacher on earth, saying, 'And you should not call anyone on earth your teacher, for one is your teacher, the Father in heaven.' (Matthew 23:9) The Father who teaches either through Himself or through Christ or in the Holy Spirit or through Paul or through Peter or through some other holy one, may it be said, only the Spirit of God and the Word of God should dwell and teach. What is this said for? Because the prophet says, 'Reveal Yourself to me, Lord, that I may know,' for I will not know unless You reveal Yourself to me, and when You reveal Yourself to me, I will see their deeds and understand what each person does and of what kind their choices are.

This is what the prophet says. Then let us see what the Savior says in the prophet: 'I was like a harmless lamb led to be sacrificed and I did not know. They plotted against me, saying, 'Come, let us put a stick into his bread, and cut him off from the land of the living, and his name will no longer be remembered.' As the prophet Isaiah says, 'The Christ was led to slaughter like a lamb, and as a sheep before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.'

There Isaiah speaks about Him, but here Christ speaks about Himself, saying, 'I was like a harmless lamb led to be sacrificed and I did not know.' He did not say what he did not know. For he did not say, 'I did not know evils,' nor 'I did not know goods,' nor 'I did not know sin,' but simply 'I did not know.' Therefore, you must investigate what He did not know. Learn what He did not know from 'The one who did not know sin, He made sin for us.' For to know sin is to commit sin, just as to know righteousness is to act righteously. Therefore, the one who announces things about righteousness and does not act righteously does not know righteousness.

english: I have abandoned my house, I have left my inheritance, I have given my beloved soul into the hands of its enemies. Behold the one existing in the form of God, who is in the heavens, behold his heavenly house. If you wish to see higher (for he is in the Father's), behold his house being God.

For that was his inheritance, the lands with the angels, the order with the holy powers. I have given my beloved soul into the hands of its enemies. english: Let us also look at the necessary rebuke next, which it is good to take up in the ethical place, saying: 'Be ashamed of your boasting, of reproach before the Lord.' (Jeremiah 9:23–24) There are things in which we boast through folly, though they are not worthy of boasting. For example, if someone boasts that he is rich and possesses much, one might say to him: 'Be ashamed of your boasting.'

If someone boasts of this outward nobility, it will be said to him: 'Be ashamed of your boasting.' If someone boasts of costly clothing, of a house built richly, that boasting is foreign to the boasting of the saints; therefore it will be said to such a one: 'Be ashamed of your boasting.' Hear the word of the prophet Jeremiah commanding us not to boast even in wisdom: 'Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom,' (Galatians 6:14) he says, 'nor the strong in his strength, nor the rich in his wealth, but let the one who boasts boast in this: understanding and knowing that I am the Lord.' (2 Corinthians 12:9) Do you want to boast and, boasting, not hear 'Be ashamed of your boasting'? Boast as the apostle and say: 'Far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through which the world has been crucified to me and I to the world.' (2 Corinthians 11:23–28) Do you want to boast so that it may not be said, 'Be ashamed of your boasting'? Hear Paul boasting and learn when he says: 'Most gladly then will I boast in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may tabernacle upon me.' Hear what kinds of boasts he boasts: 'In labors more abundantly'—which of us can say this?—'in prisons beyond measure, in deaths often.'

'Five times I received from the Jews forty lashes less one (2 Corinthians 11:24); three times I was beaten with rods; once I was stoned; three times I was shipwrecked.' So we learn that there are also differences among boastings—some boastings worthy of shame, of which that apostolic word might be said: 'And their glory is in their shame'—things of which they ought to be ashamed, and about these they suppose they are glorified.

english: Perhaps we will understand what is written by using a Gospel saying spoken by the Savior that runs like this: 'Work while it is day; night comes when no one can work.' (John 9:4) There he named day this age (but I necessarily added 'there'; for I know that other things are indicated to others elsewhere); so he named day this age, and darkness and night the consummation because of the punishments. For 'Why do you desire the day of the Lord? And this is darkness and not light,' (Amos 5:18) says Amos the prophet.

If you see what is grim after the consummation of the world—what follows as almost the whole race of human beings are punished for what was sinned—you will see that what surrounds then grew dark, and no longer can anyone glorify God, if indeed the word of God also commanded the righteous saying: 'Go, my people, enter into your storeroom, shut your door, hide yourself a little while, until my wrath of anger passes.' (Isaiah 26:20) And together with these things, if anyone can, let him observe that he said 'a little while.' But that 'little' is little to God; it is not little to a human being. For one must see that for each there is something little and great. And from an example I will show that for each there is something little or great.

For each living thing food of such-and-such amount is little by comparison with its constitution, and much food of such-and-such amount again by comparison with its makeup. And so what is little for a human being is great for another living thing. What is little, say, for a man is much for a child. So the whole time of human life is a little time, and that of one long-lived, as toward the whole of the present age. So also what is little to God is much toward us, and a whole age is God's little.

If then it is said: 'Go, my people, enter into your storerooms, shut your door, hide yourself a little while,' (Isaiah 26:20) that little must be thought said not toward the relation of the one commanded to go and enter his own storerooms, but toward the relation of the one commanding these things, to whom what is much to this one is little. For if until the wrath of God's anger passes some must enter their own storerooms, and there are those for whom sins are not forgiven not only through this whole age but also through the whole age to come, clearly that little stretches alongside what was said.

english: 'Give glory to the Lord our God before it grows dark, before your feet stumble on dark mountains.' (Psalm 87:1) There are dark mountains; there are bright mountains. Bright mountains are the holy angels of God, the prophets, Moses the servant, the apostles of Jesus Christ. All these are bright mountains, and about these I think it has been said in the Psalms: 'His foundations are in the holy mountains.' (Matthew 17:20) And what are dark mountains? Those who lift up heights against the knowledge of God.

The devil is a dark mountain; the rulers of this age who are being abolished are dark mountains; and the demon of epilepsy was a mountain, and it was a dark mountain, about which the Savior said: 'You will say to this mountain.' For when the account of epilepsy was being sought and the disciples said, 'Why could we not cast it out?' the Savior answers that 'If you have faith as a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain' (Isaiah 8:17)—about which you put forward the question, about which you sought—'You will say to this: Move from here to there, and it will move.' (Psalm 23:4) 'From here' from the human being, 'there' to its own place. So those who stumble do not stumble on bright mountains but on dark mountains, when they come to be with the devil and his angels, the dark mountains. 'And you will wait for light.' Yet it can also be joined to 'Give glory to the Lord our God'—the 'and you will wait for light.'

If you give glory to the Lord our God before it grows dark, before your feet stumble on dark mountains, clearly even if it grows dark you will wait for the light and the light will succeed you. But another might say (I do not know whether understanding soundly or not) that even those who stumble 'on dark mountains' will wait among the dark mountains waiting for the light of mercy; for this will seem to be the 'and you will wait for light.' And when someone comes upon the dark mountains, let us see what is there: 'shadow of death.'

Where the dark mountains are, there is a shadow of death generated from the dark mountains themselves. 'And they will be placed into darkness.' 'But if you do not hear in a hidden way, your soul will weep from before insult.' Of those who hear, some hear in a hidden way, and some, even if they hear, do not hear in a hidden way. What then is hearing in a hidden way but 'But we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom which God predetermined before the ages for our glory' (1 Corinthians 2:7)? And again elsewhere it is said that 'most of God's works are in hidden things.' If I hear the law, I either hear in a hidden way or I do not hear in a hidden way.

The Jew does not hear the law in a hidden way; therefore he is circumcised openly, not knowing that it is not 'the one who is a Jew openly, nor the circumcision openly in flesh.' But the one who hears circumcision in a hidden way will be circumcised in secret; the one who hears the things legislated about the Passover in a hidden way eats from the sheep of Christ—for 'our Passover was sacrificed, Christ'—and knowing what the flesh of the Word is like, and knowing that 'it is true food,' he partakes of it; for he heard the Passover in a hidden way. But this common Jew for this reason killed the Lord Jesus and is still today liable for Jesus' murder, since he heard neither the law nor the prophets in a hidden way.

If you read about the unleavened breads, one can hear the command in a hidden way, and one can hear it openly. As many of you as (for the Passover is near) keep unleavened breads, the bodily unleavened breads, you do not hear the command that says: 'If you do not hear in a hidden way, your soul will weep.' And about the Sabbath women who have not heard the prophet do not hear in a hidden way but hear openly. They do not bathe on the Sabbath day; they return 'to the poor and weak elements,' as if Christ had not sojourned—the one who perfects us and carries us across from the legal elements to the Gospel perfection.

For this reason let us attend, reading the law and the prophets, lest we fall under the prophecy that says: 'But if you do not hear in a hidden way, your soul will weep from before insult.' As many as keep the Jewish fast as not understanding the day of atonement after Jesus Christ's sojourn—you did not hear the atonement in a hidden way, but only openly; for to hear the atonement in a hidden way is to hear how God set Jesus as atonement for our sins, and that 'he is atonement for our sins, not for ours only but also for the whole world.' And even if Gospel parables are read and the hearer is one of those outside, he will not hear them in a hidden way.

But if the hearer is an apostle or one of those entering 'into Jesus' house,' he comes to Jesus, inquires also about the unclearness of the parable, and Jesus interprets it, and that hearer of the Gospel becomes one hearing it in a hidden way, so that his soul may not weep; for the soul of those not hearing in a hidden way weeps.

How marvelously he did not say: you will weep, if you do not hear in a hidden way, but: 'your soul will weep.' There is a weeping of the soul alone weeping, and perhaps the Savior teaches us that weeping when he says: 'There will be the weeping.' And even if he says: 'Woe to those who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep,' he speaks about that weeping which the prophet also threatens here saying: 'But if you do not hear in a hidden way, your soul will weep from before insult.' For when you are insulted, then you will weep and your eyes will bring down tears, because the Lord's flock was crushed. If someone now sees the Jewish things and compares them with the ancient, he will see in what way the Lord's flock was crushed.

For this was once the Lord's flock, and since they judged themselves unworthy, the word turned to the nations. If then that flock of the Lord was crushed, we the wild olive, grafted contrary to its nature into the cultivated olive of the fathers—ought we not fear more, lest this 'flock of the Lord' also be crushed? For it is going to be crushed sometime according to what was said by the Savior, when 'because lawlessness is multiplied the love of many will grow cold.' About whom is the word? Is 'the love of many will grow cold' not said about those called Christians? About whom is the word, that 'When the Son of Man comes, will he find the faith on the earth?' (Luke 18:8) Is it not about us? For this reason let us attend to ourselves, doing everything, that day by day this flock of God may be improved, healed, cured, and every crushing depart from our souls, that we may be perfected in Christ Jesus, to whom is the glory and the power forever.
Amen.

Ορᾷς τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τὸ ποτήριον τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης« οὐσαν, ὁρᾷς τὰς κολάσεις κολάσεις ποτήριον οἴνου ἀκράτου, καὶ ἄλλο εἶδος κολάσεως ποτήριον κεκερασμένον· ὥστε ἑκάστῳ κίρνασθαι κατὰ τὴν Ι άξίαν τῆς χρηστῆς πράξεως ἀναμεμιγμένης μοχθηρᾷ πράξει ἅ πίεται. νόει δέ μοι τοὺς μὲν πάντῃ ἀλλοτρίους τῆς θεοσεβείας καὶ μησαμῶς προσέχοντας αὑτοῖς, ἀλλ΄ ὡς ἔτυχε ζῶντας, πίνοντας τὸν ἄκρατον οἶνον περὶ οὗ παρεθέμεθα τὰ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἱερεμίου, τοὺς δὲ μὴ πάντῃ ἀποστάντας καὶ ἁμαρτωλούς, ἀλλ’ ἀ〈να〉ξίους τοῦ ποτηρίου «τῆς καινῆς διαθήκης«, ποιοῦντας ὁτὲ μὲν χρηστοτέρας ὁτὲ δὲ ἐναντίας πράξεις, οἶνον πίνοντας «ἀκράτου κεράσματος . «ἔκλινε« γὰρ ὁ θεὸς «ἐκ τούτου εἰς τοῦτο« τίνος «τούτου«; δύο ποτήρια βλέπω κατὰ τὸ λεγόμενον· «ἔκλινεν ἐκ τούτου εἰς τοῦτο πλὴν ὁ τρυγίας αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐξεκενώθη. νόει μοι τὸ ποτήριον τῶν ἀγαθῶν σου ἔργων ἐν τῇ μιᾷ χειρὶ τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰ δὲ βούλει τολμηρότερόν με εἰπεῖν, ἔστω ἐν τῇ χειρὶ χειρὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸ ποτήριον τῶν ἔργων σου τῶν ἀγαθῶν, εἶτα ἔστω τὸ ποτήριόν σου τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ἐν τῇ ἀριστερᾷ χειρὶ τοῦ θεοῦ.

ὅταν οὖν μέλλῃς κολάζεσθαι διὰ τὰ ἁμαρτήματα, ἐπεὶ καὶ χρηστότερά σοι ἔργα γεγένηται, ποτήριον «ἐν χειρὶ κυρίου ἐστὶν οἴνου ἀκράτου πλῆρες κεράσματος. καὶ ἔκλινεν ἐκ τούτου εἰς τοῦτο«, ἐκ τοῦ ἐν τῇ ἀριστερᾷ εἰς τὸ ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ. οὔτε γὰρ μόνον δύνασαι πιεῖν τὸ τῶν ἀγαθῶν ποτήριον, ὡς οὐ μόνον ἀγαθὰ ἔργα πεποιηκώς, οὔτε δύνασαι πιεῖν μόνον τὸ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων ποτήριον, χρηστὰ γáρ σοι πέπρακταί τινα. διὰ τοῦτο «ἔκλινεν ἐκ τούτου εἰς τοῦτο. κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῶν ἔργων σου κίρναταί σοι ὁ θυμὸς καὶ ἡ κόλασις, ἴνα ἤτοι ὑδαρέστερον τὸ τῆς κολάσεως ᾖ σοι ἢ δριμύτερον καὶ ἐπιπονώτερον. κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν γὰρ, ὡς προεῖπον, τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων συγκρινομένων τοῖς ἀγαθοῖς ἀμβλύνεταί πως ἢ οὐκ ἀμβλύνεται ὁ ἀπὸ τοῦ ποτηρίου τῆς ὁργῆς † ποσῶς διδομένης ἑκάστῳ τῶν ἁμαρτημάτων.

ἐὰν δὲ καλὸς καὶ ἀγαθὸς ᾖς ὅλος, λέγεις· «ποτήριον σωτηρίου λήψομαι, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου ἐπικαλέσομαι. «πᾶς« οὖν «ἀσκός«, εἴτε καλὸς εἴτε μοχθηρός, «πληρωθήσεται οἴνου«, καὶ κατὰ τὸν ἐπιτηδειότητα τοῦ ἀσκοῦ οἶνος βληθήσεται εἰς τὸν ἀσκὸν κατὰ τὸν λόγον τῶν ἐνταῦθα ὀνομαζομένων ἀσκῶν. ἔλαιον οὖν οὐ βάλλεται εἰς τοὺς ἀσκοὺς οὐδὲ ἄλλη τις ὑγρὰ ὕλη, ἀλλὰ πάντα ἀσκὸν δεῖ οἴνου πληρωθῆναι.
english: Consider with me then that all human beings are now, in a figurative way, able to hold wine. And I name them wineskins in this respect and say that the worthless one is filled with 'wine of the vine of Sodom,' is filled with Egyptian wine and with wine of Israel's enemies, but the holy and benefited one is filled with wine from the vine of Sorek and with wine about which it is written: 'Your cup making drunk as the strongest,' and again the holy one is filled with wine from which Wisdom has mixed. Let these things be understood by me according to vice and virtue, so that 'every wineskin is filled with wine' may be seen. But if we must also see the things that come through vice and through virtue—punishments through vice, blessings and promises through virtue—let us set out from the sacred writings how punishments and promises are called wine: 'Take the cup of this unmixed wine, and you shall make all the nations drink to whom I send you to them.' (Jeremiah 25:15)

Jeremiah says these things; to which he adds: 'And they will drink and vomit and go mad and fall.' So here he named the punishments unmixed wine, which those drink who are worthy of unmixed wine—that is, of unmixed punishment. There are also others who drink a punishment not unmixed but mixed; for 'a cup is in the Lord's hand, full of unmixed wine of mixture; he tipped from this into that; yet its dregs were not emptied out; all the sinners of the earth will drink.' If you also want to see a cup of blessing, which the righteous drink, the one of Wisdom would already suffice, at which she said: 'Drink the wine I mixed for you.' But look with me also at the Savior going up to the Passover into 'a large upper room furnished and ready,' celebrating with the disciples and giving them a cup about which it is written not that he mixed—for Jesus, gladdening the disciples, gladdens with what is unmixed—and says to them: 'Take, drink; this is my blood, poured out for you for forgiveness of sins; do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of me,' and: 'Amen I say to you, I will not drink it from now until I drink it new with you in the kingdom of God.'

You see the promise being 'the cup of the new covenant'; you see the punishments a cup of unmixed wine, and another kind of punishment a mixed cup—so that for each there is mixed, according to the worth of good practice mixed with base practice, what he will drink. Think with me of those wholly alien to piety and in no way attending to themselves, but living as it happens, drinking the unmixed wine about which we set out the things from Jeremiah; and of those not wholly fallen away and sinners, yet unworthy of the cup 'of the new covenant,' doing sometimes better and sometimes contrary deeds, drinking wine 'of unmixed mixture.' For God 'tipped from this into that'—from what 'this'? I see two cups according to the saying: 'He tipped from this into that; yet its dregs were not emptied out.' Think with me of the cup of your good works in one hand of God; and if you want me to speak more boldly, let the cup of your good works be in the right hand of God, then let the cup of your sins be in the left hand of God.

So when you are about to be punished for sins, since better works have also come to be for you, 'a cup is in the Lord's hand, full of unmixed wine of mixture. And he tipped from this into that'—from the one in the left into the one in the right. For you cannot drink only the cup of goods, as not having done only good works, nor can you drink only the cup of sins, for some good things have been done by you. Therefore 'he tipped from this into that.' According to the proportion of your works wrath and punishment are mixed for you, so that either the punishment may be more watery for you or sharper and more toilsome. For according to the proportion, as I said before, of sins compared with goods, the drink from the cup of wrath somehow grows blunt or does not grow blunt as it is given to each of the sinners.

But if you are wholly fair and good, you say: 'I will take the cup of salvation, and call on the name of the Lord.' So 'every wineskin,' whether fair or wicked, 'will be filled with wine,' and according to the fitness of the wineskin wine will be cast into the wineskin according to the account of the wineskins named here. Oil then is not cast into the wineskins, nor any other liquid matter, but every wineskin must be filled with wine.

source_text: Ἐπὶ τούτοις [τί] ἀποκρίνεται ὁ θεὸς πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τὸν κατηγορηθέντα ὑπὸ τοῦ προφήτου ἢ ὑπὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ταῦτα λέγει πρὸς αὐτόν· «σίδηρος καὶ περιβόλαιον χαλκοῦν ἡ ἰσχύς σου«, σκληρά, ἀνένδοτος, οὐκ ἐλαυνομένη. «σίδηρος καὶ περιβόλαιον χαλκοῦν ἡ ἰσχύς σου«, οἷον τμητική τις καὶ διαιροῦσα ἡ ἰσχύς σου, οὐκ ἐπ᾿ ἀγαθῷ οὖσα ἰσχύς. «καὶ θησαυρούς σου εἰς προνομὴν δώσω, ἀντάλλαγμα διὰ πάσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου. τίνας «θησαυροὺς« τῶν ἁμαρτανόντων δίδωσιν «εἰς προνομὴν« ὁ θεός, καὶ δίδωσιν αὐτοὺς «ἀντάλλαγμα διὰ πάσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας« αὐτῶν; πότερόν ποτε τοὺς ἐπὶ γῆς θησαυριζομένους αὑτοῖς; ἕκαστος γὰρ τῶν ἀνθρώπων θησαυρίζει· εἰ μὲν φαῦλός ἐστιν, ἐπὶ γῆς, εἰ δὲ ἀστεῖος, ἐν οὐρανῷ, ὡς ἐδιδάχθημεν ἀπὸ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου.

ἢ λέγει τῷ λαῷ ἐκείνῳ, ὅτι μέλλω διὰ τὰ ἁμαρτήματά σου τοὺς θησαυρούς σου διδόναι εἰς προνομήν; ποῖοι θησαυροὶ ἐκείνου τοῦ λαοῦ ἐδόθησαν εἰς προνομήν; ἴδε εἷς τῶν θησαυρῶν Ἱερεμίας, ἄλλος θησαυρὸς Ἡσαΐας, θησαυρὸς ἦν καὶ Μωσῆς. τούτους τοὺς θησαυροὺς ἔλαβεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνου τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ διὰ Χριστοῦ, εἰπόντος· «ἀρθήσεται ἀφ᾿ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς«, ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν. «Δώσω« οὖν «διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου τοὺς θησαυρούς σου εἰς προνομήν. καὶ ἔδωκεν τοὺς θησαυροὺς τοῦ λαοῦ ἐκείνου ἡμῖν· >πρῶτοι γὰρ ἐκείνοι ἐπιστεύθησαν τὰ λόγια τοῦ θεοῦ>, εἶτα μετ᾿ ἐκείνους ἡμεῖς ἐπιστεύθημεν, ἀρθέντων τῶν λογίων τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπ᾿ ἐκείνων καὶ δοθέντων ἡμῖν. καὶ λέγομεν τὸ «ἀρθήσεται ἀφ᾿ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς« εἰρῆσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος καὶ πεπληρῶσθαι. οὐχ ὅτι ἤρθη ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν ἡ γραφή, ἀλλὰ νῦν οὐκέτι ἔχυσι τὸν νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας τῷ μὴ θεωρεῖν τὸν ἐν αὐτοῖς νοῦν.

ἔχουσι γὰρ τὰ βιβλία, ἀλλὰ πῶς ἤρθη ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ; ὁ νοῦς τῶν γραφῶν ἤρθη ἀπ᾿ αὐτῶν. οὐκέτι σῴζεται διήγησις παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς νομικὴ ἢ προφηδιὰ τὴν Χριστοῦ ἐπιδημίαν τὸ «εἶπον τῷ λαῷ ἐκείνῳ· ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.

ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου. πεπλήρωται καὶ τὸ εἰρημένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου ὅτι «ἀφελεῖ κύριος ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἰσχύοντα καὶ ἰσχύουσαν, γίγαντα καὶ πολεμιστὴν ἄνθρωπον, σικαστὴν καὶ προφήτην καὶ στοχαστὴν καὶ σοφὸν ἀρχιτέκτονα καὶ συνετὸν ἀκροατην. ταῦτα πάντα ἀφεῖλεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνων καὶ ἔδωκεν, ἐάν γε ἡμεῖς δεξώμεθα, ἡμῖν τοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν. ταῦτα διὰ τὸ «καὶ τοὺς θησαυρούς σου εἰς ἁρονομὴν δώσω. «Ἀντάλλαγμα διὰ πάσας τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς ὁρίοις σου.

ὡσεὶ ἔλεγε· διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου τὰς ἐπὶ πάντα τὰ ὅριά σου ἐφθακυίας· οὐδὲν γὰρ ὅριον ἐκείνου τοῦ λαοῦ ἐστιν, ὅ ἁμαρτίας οὐ πεπλήρωται. καὶ πῶς πᾶν ὅριον αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔμελλεν ἁμαρτίας πληροῦσθαι [ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς], τὸ ὅσον ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἀποκτεινάντων δικαιοσύνην, εἰ Χριστὸς δικαιοσύνη, ἀποκτεινάντων [τὴν] σοφίαν, εἰ Χριστὸς σοφία, ἀποκτεινάντων ἀλήθειαν, εἰ Χριστὸς ἀλήθεια; διὰ γὰρ τοῦ καταδεδικακέναι τὴν ἐπὶ θανάτῳ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ταῦτα πάντα ἀπέβαλον καὶ ἀπώλεσαν. καὶ ἀναστάς μου ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἐν νεκρῶν οὐκέτι ἐφάνη τοῖς ἀποκτείνασιν αὐτόν· οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ἐν τῇ ἱστορίᾳ ὅτι ἐφάνη τοῖς ἀποκτείνασιν αὐτόν, ἀλλὰ μόνοις τοῖς πιστεύουσιν ἐφάνη ἀναστὰς ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν.
english: Upon these things God answers toward the people accused by the prophet or by Christ and says these things to him: 'Iron and a bronze covering is your strength'—hard, unyielding, not driven. 'Iron and a bronze covering is your strength'—as if your strength were some cutting and dividing force, not being strength for good. 'And I will give your treasures into plunder, an exchange for all your sins.' Which 'treasures' of those who sin does God give 'into plunder,' and give them 'as exchange for all their sins'? Is it sometime those stored up for themselves on earth? For each of humans stores up; if he is base, on earth, but if noble, in heaven, as we were taught from the Gospel.

Or does he say to that people that because of your sins I am about to give your treasures into plunder? What sorts of treasures of that people were given into plunder? See: one of the treasures was Jeremiah, another treasure Isaiah; Moses too was a treasure. God took these treasures from that people and through Christ, who said: 'The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits,' (Matthew 21:43) gave them to us. So 'I will give because of your sins your treasures into plunder.' And he gave that people's treasures to us; for 'first they were entrusted with the oracles of God,' then after them we were entrusted, the oracles of God having been taken from them and given to us. And we say that 'The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits' was spoken by the Savior and has been fulfilled—not that the writing was taken from them, but now they no longer have the law and the prophets by not seeing the mind in them.

For they have the books, but how was the kingdom of God taken from them? The mind of the Scriptures was taken from them. No longer is a legal or prophetic interpretation saved among them, because of Christ's sojourn, the 'I said to that people: Hearing you will hear and will not understand, and seeing you will see and will not perceive.'

For the heart of this people was made fat. And what was said by Isaiah has also been fulfilled: that 'The Lord will take away from Judea and from Jerusalem the strong man and the strong woman, giant and warrior man, judge and prophet and diviner and wise master-builder and intelligent hearer.' God took all these away from them and gave them—if at least we receive—to us from the nations. These things because of 'And I will give your treasures into plunder. An exchange for all your sins and in all your borders.'

As if he said: because of your sins that have reached upon all your borders; for there is no border of that people that has not been filled with sin. And how would every border of theirs not be about to be filled with sin—as far as it lay with them—who killed righteousness, if Christ is righteousness; who killed wisdom, if Christ is wisdom; who killed truth, if Christ is truth? For through condemning the Son of God to death they cast off and destroyed all these. And my Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, no longer appeared to those who killed him; for we do not have in the history that he appeared to those who killed him, but only to those who believe did he appear risen from the dead.

source_text: «γνῶθι ὡς ἔλαβον περὶ σοῦ ὀνειδισμὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀθετούντων τοὺς λόγους σου. ἔστω ὁ προφήτης, λέγων καὶ ἐξουθενημένος ἐφ᾿ οἷς ἔλεγεν, ὑπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν ἀθετούμενος· φησὶ γὰρ αὐτός· «διετέλεσα μυκτηριζόμενος. ὠνειδίζετο οὖν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀθετούντων τοὺς λόγους τοὺς δι᾿ αὐτοῦ λαλουμένους ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ εὔχεται ἐπὶ τῷ ὠνειδίσθαι βοηθηθῆναι ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ λέγων· «γνῶθι ὡς ἔλαβον περὶ σοῦ ὀνειδισμὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀθε- τούντων τοὺς λόγους σου· συντέλεσον αὐτούς. λεγέτω ὁ προφήτης, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον ἁρμόζει τὸ «συντέλεσον αὐτοὺς« λεγόμενον ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· συντέλεια γὰρ ἦλθε περὶ τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῷ λαῷ, ἐπὶ τοῖς συμβεβηκόσιν ἐξ ἐπιβουλῆς τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν.

Μετὰ ταῦτα ἀναγκαῖον διὰ τὸ πολλὰ πεπονθέναι τοὺς προφήτας ἐλέγχοντας καὶ τὸν λόγον πρεσβεύοντας καὶ λαβοῦντας τὰ προστασ· σόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑπομνῆσαι τοὺς ἀκροατὰς περὶ τοῦ βίου αὐτῶν καὶ τῶν ἐπαγγελιῶν αὐτῶν καὶ τῆς ἡμετέρας προαιρέσεως, ἵνα κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἡμῖν, εἰ θέλομεν μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν ἔχειν ἀνάπαυσιν, τὰ ἔργα τῶν προφητῶν ζηλώσωμεν.

ὅ δὲ λέγω τοιοῦτόν ἐστι· πολλάκις ἐν ταῖς εὐχαῖς λέγομεν· θεὲ παντοκράτορ, τὴν μερίδα ἡμῶν μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν δός, τὴν μερίδα ἡμῶν μετὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων τοῦ Χριστοῦ σου δός, ἵνα εὑρεθῶμεν καὶ μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ. ταῦτα δὲ λέγοντες οὐκ αἰσθανόμεθα τί εὐχόμεθα· δυνάμει γὰρ τοῦτό φαμεν· δὸς ἡμᾶς παθεῖν ἃ πεπόνθασιν οἱ προφῆται, δὸς καὶ ἡμᾶς μισηθῆναι ὡς ἐμισήθησαν οἱ προφῆται, λόγους τοιούτους δὸς ἐφ᾿ οἷς μισηθησόμεθα, δὸς τοσαύταις περιστάσεσι περιπεσεῖν ὅσαις οἱ ἀπόστολοι. τὸ γὰρ λέγειν· δός μοι μερίδα μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν, μὴ παθόντα τὰ τῶν προφητῶν μηδὲ παθεῖν θέλοντα ἄδικόν ἐστι. τὸ λέγειν· δός μοι μερίδα μετὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων, μὴ θέλοντα ἀπὸ διαθέσεως Παύλου ἀληθεύοντα εἰπεῖν· «ἐν κόποις περισσοτέρως, ἐν πληγαῖς περισσοτέρως, ἐν φυλακαῖς ὑπερβαλλόντως, ἐν θανάτοις πολλάκις« καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς, πάντων ἐστὶν ἀδικώτατον. εἴπερ οὖν θέλομεν μετὰ τῶν προφητῶν γενέσθαι, ὅρα τοὺς βίους τῶν προφητῶν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ ἐλέγχειν, ἐκ τοῦ ἐπιτιμᾶν, ἐκ τοῦ ἐπιπλήσσειν ἐδικάζοντο, διεκρίνοντο, κατεδικάζοντο. «ἐλιθάσθησαν, ἐπρίσθησαν, ἐπειράσθησαν, ἐν φόνῳ μαχαίρας ἀπέθανον, περιῆλθον ἐν μηλωταῖς, ἐν αἰγείοις δέρμασιν, ὑστερούμενοι, θλιβόμενιο, κακουχούμενοι, ἐπ᾿ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι«, ὅτε συναγωγαὶ πολλαὶ Ἰουδαίων· καὶ οὖτοι ἦσαν «ἐπ᾿ ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς. τί οὖν παράδοξον, εἰ θέλων τις ξηλοῦν τὸν βίον τὸν προφητικόν, ἐλέγχων, ἐπιπλήσσων τὸν ἁμαρτάνοντα κακολογεῖται, μισεῖται, ἐπιβουλεύεται; ὥσπερ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος ἔδει † γενέσθαι τοιοῦτον εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ. κατεγνώσθη ὁ καταγνωσθείς, ὁ δεῖνα † καθεζόμενος ἐποίει τὰ τοιάσε· ἔδει γενέσθαι ἐκκλη- σιατικὴν ἐκδικίαν, καὶ γέγονεν· πεποίηκεν ὁ ἐγκεχειρισμένος τὸ ἔργον ὃ ἔδει αὐτὸν πεποιηκέναι. περιέρχεται ἐκεῖνος λέγων κακῶς τὸν ἐκδικήσαντα τὴν ἀλήθειαν. ἀλλ᾿ ἡμεῖς τοῦτο μὴ ποιῶμεν, μὴ παρέχωμεν τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῖς διὰ τὸ ἐκβεβλῆσθαι λέγουσι κακῶς τὸν ἐκβαλόντα ἢ τὸν σύμψηφον γενόμενον. οἱ καὶ ἀδικίας γε ἐλεγχομένης καὶ γεγενημένης †. οἱ θαυμάσιοι ἀπόστολοι μυρία ὑβριζόμενοι διὰ τὴν ἀλήθειαν λέγουσιν· «εὐδοκῶ ἐν ἀσθενείαις, ἐν ὕβρεσι καὶ ἀνάγκαις, ἐν διωγμοῖς καὶ στενοχωρίαις, ὑπὲρ Χριστοῦ. μόνον εἴη με ὑβριζόμενον εἰδέναι ὅτι οὐ δἰ ἄλλο τι ὑβρίζομαι ἢ διὰ Χριστόν, ἐν ἀνάγκαις γενόμενον εἰδέναι ὅτι ἡ ὑπόθεσις τῶν ἀναγκαίων ὁ Χριστός ἐστιν. εἴη με λοιδορούμενον εἰδέναι ὅτι ἡ πρόφασις τῆς λοιδορίας οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλη, ἢ ὅτι ἐκδικῶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν καὶ πρεσβεύω ὑπὲρ τῶν γεγραμμένων, ἵωα κατὰ λόγον θεοῦ πάντα γίνηται, διὰ τοῦτο βλασφημοῦμαι. καὶ ἡμεῖς οὖν πάντες, ὅση δύναμις, σπεύσωμεν ἐπὶ τὸν βίον τὸν προφητικόν, ἐπὶ τὸν βίον τὸν ἀποστολικόν, τὸ ὀχληρὸν μὴ φεύγοντες· ἀθλητὴς γὰρ ἐὰν φύγῃ τὸ τῆς ἀθλήσεως ὀχληρόν, τὸ ἡδὺ τοῦ στεφάνου οὐκ ἀπολήφεται.
english: 'Know that I received reproach concerning you from those who set aside your words.' (Jeremiah 20:7) Let the prophet, speaking and made nothing of for what he said, be set aside by sinners; for he himself says: 'I continued being mocked.' So he was reproached by those who set aside the words spoken through him by God, and he prays, upon being reproached, to be helped by God saying: 'Know that I received reproach concerning you from those who set aside your words; finish them.' (Hebrews 11:37) Let the prophet say it, but 'finish them' spoken by the Savior fits better; for a finishing came upon Jerusalem and the people, upon what happened from the people's plot against our Savior.

After these things it is necessary—because the prophets suffered much convicting and ambassadoring the word and taking what was commanded by God—to remind the hearers about their life and their promises and our choice, so that as far as we can, if we want to have rest with the prophets, we may zealously imitate the prophets' works.

What I mean is like this: often in prayers we say: Almighty God, give our portion with the prophets, give our portion with the apostles of your Christ, that we may also be found with Christ himself. And saying these things we do not perceive what we pray; for in effect we say this: grant us to suffer what the prophets suffered, grant us also to be hated as the prophets were hated, give such words for which we will be hated, grant us to fall into as many circumstances as the apostles. For to say 'give me a portion with the prophets' (2 Corinthians 12:9–10) while neither having suffered the prophets' things nor wanting to suffer is unjust. To say 'give me a portion with the apostles' while not wanting from Paul's disposition, speaking truly, to say: 'In toils more abundantly, in blows more abundantly, in prisons beyond measure, in deaths often' and what follows, is most unjust of all. If then we want to come to be with the prophets, look at the prophets' lives—that from convicting, from rebuking, from striking they were judged, examined, condemned. 'They were stoned, they were sawn, they were tested, they died by murder of sword, they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, lacking, afflicted, mistreated, wandering upon deserts' (Hebrews 11:37–38)—when there were many synagogues of Jews; and these were 'wandering upon deserts and mountains and caves and the holes of the earth.' What then is strange if someone wanting to zealously imitate the prophetic life, convicting, striking the one who sins, is spoken ill of, hated, plotted against? Just as also in the present such a thing had to come to be into God's church. The one who was condemned was condemned; so-and-so sitting did such things; there had to be church vindication, and it came to be; the one entrusted with the work did what he ought to have done. That one goes about speaking ill of the one who vindicated the truth. But let us not do this; let us not lend our ears to those who, because they have been cast out, speak ill of the one who cast out or of the one who became a fellow voter. The marvelous apostles, insulted countless times because of the truth, say: 'I am well pleased in weaknesses, in insults and necessities, in persecutions and distresses, for Christ.' Only may I, being insulted, know that I am insulted for no other reason than for Christ; coming into necessities, know that the ground of the necessities is Christ. May I, being abused, know that the pretext of the abuse is no other than that I vindicate the truth and ambassador for what is written, so that according to God's word everything may come to be—for this reason I am blasphemed. So let us all too, as much strength as there is, hasten upon the prophetic life, upon the apostolic life, not fleeing what is burdensome; for if an athlete flees the burdensome of the contest, he will not receive the pleasant of the crown.

source_text: «Κατὰ μόνας ἐκαθήμην. καὶ τὰ ῥήματα ἐνταῦθα οἰκοκομεῖ. ὅταν πλῆθος ᾖ ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ μὴ φέρωσι τὸν δίκαιον βιοῦντα | δικαίως, οὐδὲν ἄτοπόν ἐστι φεύγοντα τὸ συνέδριον τῆς κακίας μιμήσασθαι τὸν εἰπόντα· «κατὰ μόνας ἐκαθήμην«, μιμήσασθαι καὶ τὸν λέγοντα Ἡλίαν· «κύριε, τοὺς προφήτας σου ἀπέκτειναν, τὰ θυσιαστήριά σου κατέσκαψαν, κἀγῶ ὑπελείφθην μονώτατος, καὶ ζητοῦσι τὴν ψυχῆν μου λαβεῖν αὐτήν. τάχα δὲ κἂν βαθύτερον ἐξετάσῃς τὸ «κατὰ μόνας ἐκαθήμην«, εὑρήσεις τινὰ ἄξιον νοῦν βάθους προφητικοῦ. ὅταν τὸν τῶν πολλῶν βίον μμιμώμεθα, ὥστε μὴ εἶναι ἀνακεχωρηκότα αὐτὸν καὶ κρείττονα καὶ ἐξαίρετον παρὰ τοὺς πολλούς, οὐ δύναμαι λέγειν· «κατὰ μόνας ἐκαθήμην«, ἀλλά· μετὰ πολλῶν ἐκαθήμην.

ἐπὰν δὲ ὁ βίος μου γένηται δυσμίμητος, ὥστε με τηλικοῦτον γενέσθαι, ὡς μηδένα παραπλήσιον εἶναί μου τῷ ἤθει, τῷ λόγῳ, ταῖς πράξεσι, τῇ σοφίᾳ, τότε δύναμαι λέγειν παὰ τὸ μόνος εἶναι τοιόσδε καὶ μηδένα μιμήσασθαί με τὸ «κατὰ μμόνας ἐκθήμην.

ἔξεστιν οὖν καὶ μὴ ὄντα σε πρεσβύτερον καὶ μὴ ὄντα σε ἐπίσκοπον μηδέ τινι τιμῇ ἐκκλησιαστικῇ τετιμημένον εἰπεῖν τοῦτο, τὸ «κατὰ μόνας ἐκαθή΄μην« ζηλῶσαι καὶ βίον ἀναλαβεῖν ὥστε εἰπεὶν· «κατὰ μόνας ἐκαθήμην. «Ὅτι πικρίας ἐνεπλήσθην. εἰ «στενὴ καὶ τεθλιμμένη ἡ ὁδὸς ἡ ἑορτή σου μετὰ πικρίδων γίνεται; ὅταν γὰρ ἑορτάζῃς, «ἄζυμα« φησὶν «ἐπὶ πικρίδων φάγεσαι. τί βούλεται ὁ λόγος λέγων ὅτι δεὶ τὸν ἑορτάζοντα τῷ θεῷ «ἄζυμα ἐπὶ πικρίδων« ἐσθίειν, κατανοητέον. τὰ μὲν ἄζυμα διηγήσατο ὁ ἀπόστολος, οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὴ ἡ ἑρμηνεία· τὸ δὲ ἀκόλουθον τῆς ἑρμηνείας ἀναγκαῖόν ἐστι παραπλήσιον εἶναι τῇ ἀποστολικῇ διηγήσει.

ὁ ἀπόστολος τὰ περὶ τῶν ἀζύμων διηγήσατο λέγων· «ἑορτάζωμεν μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας καὶ πονηρίας, ἀλλ᾿ ἐν ἀζύμοις εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας. δέον ἐστὶν ἀποδοῦναι τὸν λόγον περὶ τῶν πικρίδων ἀκολούθως τῷ τὰ ἄζυμα εῑναι εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας. ἔχε δὲ εἰλικρίνειαν καὶ ἀλήθειαν, καὶ πικρίδες ἔσονταί σοι, καὶ ἐσθίεις μετὰ πικρίδων τὰ ἄζυμα τῆς εἰλικρινείας καὶ ἀληθείας, οἷον Παῦλος. ἐπειδήπερ ἤσθιε τὰ ἄζυμα εἰλικοινείας καὶ ἀληθείας, καὶ πικρίδας ἤσθιε. πῶς πικρίδας ἤσθιε; λέγων «ἐχθρὸς ὑμῶν γέγονα ἀληθεύων ὑμῖν. πῶς πικρίδας ἤσθιεν; «ἐν κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ, καὶ ἐν ἀγρυπνίαις πολλάκις, ἐν λιμῷ καὶ δίψει, χωρὶς τῶν παρεκτός.

ὁ μὲν οὖν νόμος εἶπεν· 〉ἄζυμα μετὰ πικρίδων ἔδεσθε ἔδεσθε〈· καὶ οὐκ εἶπεν· ἄζυμα μετὰ πικρίδων ἔδεσθε, ἕως ἐμπλησθῆτε, ὥσπερ ἐπί τινων ἄλλων λέλεκται· «φάγεσθε καὶ ἐμπλησθήσεσθε. ὁ δὲ προφήτης προσεπιτείνει λέγων ὅτι οὐχὶ πικρίαν ἔφαγον, ἀλλὰ «πικρίας ἐνεπλήσθην«· ὅση δύναμις τῶν πικρῶν μετελάμβανον πραγμάτων, ὥστε με[τὰ] πληρεστάτων πικρίδων μεταλβεῖν.
english: 'I was sitting alone.' And the words are managed here. Whenever there is a multitude of sinners and they do not bear the righteous living righteously, it is not out of place for one fleeing the council of wickedness to imitate the one who said: 'I was sitting alone,' to imitate also Elijah who says: 'Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have dug down your altars, and I alone have been left, and they seek my soul to take it.' (1 Kings 19:10, 14) And perhaps even if you examine more deeply 'I was sitting alone,' you will find some mind worthy of prophetic depth. Whenever we imitate the life of the many, so as not to be withdrawn and better and exceptional beside the many, I cannot say: 'I was sitting alone,' but: I was sitting with many.

But when my life becomes hard to imitate, so that I become so great that no one is near me in character, in word, in deeds, in wisdom, then I can say—because of being alone such and no one imitating me—'I was sitting alone.'

So it is possible even if you are not an elder and not a bishop and not honored with some church honor to say this, to zealously imitate 'I was sitting alone' and take up a life so as to say: 'I was sitting alone.' 'Because I was filled with bitternesses.' (1 Kings 19:10) If 'narrow and afflicted is the way,' how does your feast come to be with bitter herbs? For when you feast, it says 'you shall eat unleavened breads upon bitter herbs.' (Exodus 12:8; Num 9:11) What the word wants saying that the one feasting to God must eat 'unleavened breads upon bitter herbs' (Galatians 4:16) must be considered. The apostle interpreted the unleavened breads; the interpretation is not mine; but what follows of the interpretation must necessarily be near the apostolic interpretation.

The apostle interpreted the things about the unleavened breads saying: 'Let us feast not in old leaven nor in leaven of wickedness and evil, but in unleavened breads of sincerity and truth.' (1 Corinthians 5:8) It is necessary to give the account about the bitter herbs following upon the unleavened breads being of sincerity and truth. Have sincerity and truth, and bitter herbs will be yours, and you eat with bitter herbs the unleavened breads of sincerity and truth—as Paul. Since he ate the unleavened breads of sincerity and truth, he also ate bitter herbs. How did he eat bitter herbs? Saying 'I have become your enemy speaking truly to you.' How did he eat bitter herbs? 'In toil and labor, and in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, apart from the things besides.' (2 Corinthians 11:27–28)

So the law said: 'You shall eat unleavened breads with bitter herbs'; and it did not say: you shall eat unleavened breads with bitter herbs until you are filled, as upon certain other things it has been said: 'You shall eat and be filled.' But the prophet presses further saying that I did not eat bitterness, but 'I was filled with bitternesses'; as much strength as there was I partook of bitter affairs, so as to partake with the fullest bitter herbs.

english: 'My wound is hard; from where will I be healed?' (Acts 3:21) Those who overpower me strike me, and my wound is hard. Whether he prophesies the Lord's cross (for the cross is a hard wound, as far as it lies with those who crucify him), or whether it is said about all the righteous in whom he receives a hard wound, or even if you hear this upon the prophet (for he too suffered the things written in the prophecy), it admits the same sense according to the wording that says: 'My wound is hard.' 'From where will I be healed?' Even if the Savior says: 'From where will I be healed?' he prophesies the resurrection from the dead after the hard wound; and even if it is taken upon the righteous, after the wounds healing comes again. 'Coming to be it became for me as false water, not having faith'; for the wound does not remain but passes. 'Therefore thus says the Lord: If you turn, I will also restore you.' These things are said again toward each whom God will call to turn toward him. And a mystery seems to me to be announced here in the 'I will restore you.' No one is restored into some place never having been there at all, but restoration is into what is one's own. For example if a limb of mine becomes dislocated, the physician tries to make a restoration of the dislocation.

Whenever someone comes to be outside the fatherland, whether justly or unjustly, and then receives again the power to be in the fatherland according to the laws, he was restored upon his own fatherland. Think the same with me also upon a soldier cast out from his own battle-line and being restored. So here he says toward us who turned away that, if we turn, he will restore us. For the end of the promise is also such, as it is written in the Acts of the Apostles in the 'until times of restoration of all things which God spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from of old' (Acts 3:21) in Christ Jesus, to whom is the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.

english: But I need an example, that I may show how it is possible, having come upon an angel, to see God through an angel. For it is written in Exodus: 'An angel of the Lord appeared to Moses in a flame of fire from a bush.' And Moses sees that the bush burns with fire, and the bush is not consumed. And Scripture did not say, as it said at the beginning that 'an angel appeared,' that thus it remained only an angel of the Lord, but: 'I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob.' So God was there being contemplated in the angel, as God is known through the rock and through the hole in it.

You do not know, then, when the hunters are sent. For this reason never come down from the mountains, nor leave the hills, nor be outside the clefts of the rocks; for if you are found outside, it will be said to you as to one who is outside and saying the things of those outside: 'Fool, this night they require your soul from you; and the things you prepared, whose will they be?' And these things will also be said to you if you say: 'I will pull down my storehouses and build greater ones, and I will say to my soul: Soul, you have goods laid up for many years; rest, eat, drink, be merry.'

You see the one below the mountains, below the hills, outside the clefts of the rocks, how he wanders even in the judgment about goods, thinking these things are goods. Therefore he says: 'And I will say to my soul: Soul, you have goods laid up for many years.' (Luke 12:19) He has judged the grain and the abundance of earthly things to be goods; for he did not see that the truly good things are not in the cursed earth, but the truly good things are in heaven. He was treasuring on earth, because he thought the things on earth were goods. But if someone turns from treasuring 'on earth,' persuaded by Jesus, to treasuring 'in heaven,' it will not be said to him: 'Fool, this night they require your soul from you,' but the hunters, coming and seeking not the things below but the living things in the mountains, in the hills, those sheltered in the clefts of the rocks, will seize them and lead them away from that hunt—where?—to the rest of the holy and blessed in Christ Jesus.

For 'my eyes,' he says, 'are upon all their ways.' Upon such as these—those who make their sojourns upon the mountains and in the hills and in the clefts of the rocks—God has his eyes upon all the ways. 'And they were not hidden from my face'—such as these; for the base hide from the face of God. Adam, after the transgression, heard 'the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the afternoon' (Genesis 3:8) and hid; but the holy one is not hidden, but has a heart with boldness toward God according to the holy way of life. For 'if our conscience does not condemn us, we have boldness toward God, and whatever we ask we receive from him.' Adam, then, even if he sinned, did not sin unto an exceedingly harsh sin; for this reason he hid from the face of God. But Cain, more sinful than he and most impious, the brother-killer—what did he do? 'He went out from the face of God.' So that by comparison of evils, to hide from the face of God is the lesser; for even this one hides not brazenly, but ashamed before God. 'They were not hidden,' then, 'from my face.' These who have done these things were once in sins and were fished from the sins that were in the sea.

english: 'If anyone among you seems to himself to be wise in this age, let him become a fool.' (1 Corinthians 3:18) Attend: he did not only cry, 'Be a fool and senseless,' but 'that you may become wise.' If therefore there is a blameworthy wisdom, according to which 'the sons of this age are wiser than the sons of light in this generation,' God is good, who overturns diversities by contraries, that what was said may be fulfilled: 'his end will be a fool.'

When will his end be a fool? It is necessary that Christ 'reign until God puts all his enemies under his feet'; and when he has subjected all things to him, 'the last enemy, death, will be destroyed.' When death has been destroyed, then will be the utmost of the partridge, and his end will become a fool. These things about the partridge.

The beginning of the second chapter that was read is this: 'A throne of glory exalted from the beginning is the place of our sanctification; our endurance, the endurance of Israel. Lord, all who have forsaken you shall be confounded; departing, they shall be written upon the earth, because they have forsaken the fountain of life, the Lord.' Isaiah the blessed prophet, seeing the Lord and his kingdom, said: 'I saw the Lord of hosts sitting upon a throne high and lifted up.' Jeremiah also saw how God reigns; therefore glorifying him he says: 'A throne of glory exalted from the beginning is the place of our sanctification.'

Whether you wish to understand these things of Christ, you will not err; or of the Father, you will not think impiously: for the Savior is a throne of glory high and from the beginning. 'Throne of glory,' because his kingdom is high; and 'our sanctification' is Christ; for 'he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one.' 'Endurance of Israel': just as the Savior is absolute righteousness, absolute truth, absolute sanctification, so also absolute endurance. And it is not possible to be righteous apart from Christ, nor holy apart from him, nor to endure without having Christ. For he himself is the endurance of Israel. And if you refer it to God, not even so do you go wrong.

english: 'Behold, they say to me: Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come. But I did not grow weary following after you.' (Matthew 16:24) Jesus says to you: 'Take up your cross and follow me,' and 'Leave all things and follow me,' and 'Whoever does not leave father and mother and follow after me is not worthy to be my disciple.' (Matthew 19:21) If then you become such that you always follow Jesus, you will also follow, and as long as you follow you will not grow weary; for 'there will be no toil in Jacob, nor will pain be seen in Israel.' (Matthew 10:37–38) There is no labor for the one following Jesus; the very following takes away the labor.

Therefore he himself says, so that we may no longer grow weary—having grown weary before we began to follow him: 'Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.' (Matthew 11:28) If then, laboring, we come to him and follow him, we will say: 'But I did not grow weary following after you.'

And it is consequent for us to say also: 'I did not desire a human day.' There is a day of a human, and there is a day of God. Let each of us desire the day of the resurrection of the holy ones, not that day concerning which it is written: 'Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord; and this is darkness and not light.' Who is the one who says: 'And I did not desire a human day'? The clarity of the word will convict us that we have desired a human day. Often when we have fallen sick and come into a fantasy of death, at the departure we beg the brothers who watch over us and say: Ask for me a leave, ask for me to remain in life. Saying these things we do not desire a holy day of God, but a human day. Therefore putting away love of the body and the desire for a human day, let us seek to see that day in which we will obtain the blessedness in Christ Jesus, to whom be the glory and the power unto the ages. Amen.

ἐγὼ δὲ γενόμενος κατὰ τὸν τόπον καὶ τοιαῦτά τινα εἴποιμι ἂν ὅ ἐὰν λέγῃ μοι ὁ ὄφις, κἂν ἀληθῆ μοι λέγῃ κἂν ἀπατᾶν με θέλῃ, ὑφορῶμαι αὐτοῦ τοὺς λόγους πειθόμενος ὅτι, εἴτε ἀπατᾷ με εἴτε ἀληθεύει, βλάπτει με. καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια γὰρ αὐτοῦ βλάπτει· οὐδὲν ὠφέλιμον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄφεως γίνεται, ἐπεὶ >μὴ δύναται δένδρον πονηρὸν καρποὺς, ἀγαθοὺς ἐνεγκεῖν<.

english: I want to take a risk and give an example of those benefited while deceived. There are some who practice chastity and purity for this reason, and others who practice single marriage for this reason, because they expected the one who has marital intercourse to perish, and the one who marries twice to perish. Let us compare among ourselves: what benefits the single-married—to be deceived and think the twice-married is punished and handed over to eternal punishment, that she may remain single-married and pure—or to know the truth and marry twice? I think anyone seeing what follows can say that it would have been more blessed to be pure and not marry twice without being deceived, and to see that the twice-married shares some salvation, yet not so great a blessedness as the one who, though able to marry twice, stayed pure. But if she cannot do this, it is better to be deceived as if the twice-married perish and through the deception stay pure, than to know the truth and come into the lesser rank of the twice-married. You will find something such also among those practicing chastity and complete purity.

And many other things would be found done by us according to a deception and benefiting us. But how many supposed wise, having found the truth about punishment and having passed through the things of the deception, have come into a worse life? It would have benefited them to think as they thought before about 'their worm will not die' and that 'their fire will not be quenched' and that 'they will be for a sight to all flesh' and that 'the chaff will be burned with unquenchable fire.' But if imagining something else beside their first notion they are about to despise 'the wealth of the kindness of God and the forbearance and the long-suffering,' see whether truly for this reason, because they did not seem to have been deceived, they stored up for themselves 'wrath in a day of wrath and revelation and just judgment of God'—which they would not have stored if they had been deceived. These things because of the deception from God, since the prophet said: 'You deceived me, Lord, and I was deceived.'

And let us also pass privately into 'I was deceived.' Why did he not say only 'You deceived me, Lord,' but also added 'and I was deceived'? Sometimes one can conceive someone working the deception, but another being on guard against being deceived and not being deceived. But when the one works the deceiving and the other does not guard against being deceived but falls into the deception, he would say: 'You deceived me, Lord, and I was deceived.' And I, coming to be at the place, would also say something such: if the serpent says something to me, whether he says true things or wants to deceive me, I am suspicious of his words, persuaded that whether he deceives me or speaks truly he harms me. For even his truth harms; nothing beneficial comes from the serpent, since 'a bad tree cannot bear good fruits.' (Matthew 7:18)
